newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese not active buyers of US Q4 corn--traders.
newsitem.headline: Japanese not active buyers of US Q4 corn--traders.

text.p: Some Japanese grain importers are buying U.S. corn for October-December shipment, but most are waiting for a better time to buy, local traders said on Thursday.
On Wednesday, the CBOT corn futures market closed higher with commercial buying in the December cited as one reason, traders said.
The buying in the December led to talk that importers may be pricing some of their new crop corn import needs, the traders said.
"It's about the time to cover U.S. corn for the fourth quarter, and some traders are already buying," a corn trader at a major trade house said.
"But most traders are waiting for further drops in corn prices to return to the market," he said.
China -- another major corn supplier -- is still offering corn to Japan, but its prices are too high to attract Japanese buyers, the traders said.

China earlier this year was offering corn at about $135 per tonne at the port of Dalian. "They've been cutting offer prices gradually because Japanese buyers are so reluctant to buy," another corn trader in Tokyo said.
